newsitem.title: CHINA: SWIMMING-CHINA DOMINATE WORLD CUP WITH GOLD HAUL.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-CHINA DOMINATE WORLD CUP WITH GOLD HAUL.

text.p: China's women swimmers continued to dominate the World Cup short-course series by capturing five gold medals in the second leg in Beijing on Wednesday.
The Chinese squad was led by 17-year-old Chen Yan, who powered her way to gold in the 200 metres individual medley and the 200 metres backstroke.

Team mate Shan Ying took the title in the 50 metre freestyle, Han Xie won the 100 metres breaststroke and Liu Limian triumphed with a time of 59.07 seconds in the 100 metres butterfly, still shy of her world record 58.68.

The Chinese assault was partly countered by Olympic gold medallist Claudia Poll of Costa Rica, who won the 200 metres freestyle, and by Russia's Nina Zhyvanevskaya, who clinched a narrow .04 second win in the 50 metres backstroke.
Poll's one minute 57.02 seconds timing was well short of her world record 1:55.42.
Taiwan's Lin Chi-chan kept Poll from repeating her twin gold feat from the World Cup's first leg in Hong Kong by edging the Costa Rican in the 800 metres freestyle.
China's gold medallist at the Atlanta Olympics and world record-holder Le Jingyi did not appear in Wednesday's event.
The Chinese squad is seeking to re-establish its world dominance after seven swimmers were banned in an embarrassing doping scandal after the 1994 Asian Games.

China's Lu Bin, swimming in her first international event since she was suspended in the Asian Games scandal, put in a disappointing performance, failing to make the top three in both the 50 metres and 200 metres backstroke.
The Chinese men's team also put in a strong showing with three golds while the Netherlands' one-man squad represented by Marcel Wouda landed two titles.
Zeng Qiliang came out on top in the 50 metres breaststroke, Xiong Guoming came from behind to touch first in the 400 metres freestyle, and Zhang Qiang won the 50 metres butterfly.
Wouda scored his golds in the 400 metres and 100 metres individual medleys.
Adrian Radley secured gold for Australia with his win in the 100 metres backstroke while Sion Brinn of Jamaica took the 100 metres freestyle.
Espoo in Finland is the scene of the third leg of the competition starting on January 22. Total prize money of $150,000 awaits the winners of the eight-round event.
